do_more: Use classic public‑domain psychology titles (e.g., original book name and author) as the video hook
Keep titles concise, no emojis, and include a clear reference to the source material
Aim for a ~42‑second runtime (standard length) to allow a full, engaging excerpt
Open with a striking quote or question from the text to capture curiosity
Maintain a calm, authoritative narration style matching the vintage content
avoid: Clickbait emojis or modern slang in titles and thumbnails
Cover overly generic trending topics that aren’t tied to classic works
Produce ultra‑short <30‑second cuts that truncate the reading
Use flashy, unrelated visuals that break the vintage aesthetic
short.title_style: Use the original work’s title and author as a clear, authoritative hook—e.g., “The Expression of the Emotions in Man and Animals – Chapter 3”.
next_tests: Test tight 30‑second edits of the same classic excerpt against the 42‑second standard version
Add an on‑screen citation of the original author/book to see if shares increase
Launch a “Reading X” series without emojis but with consistent branding to gauge binge‑ability

do_more: Pick concrete, everyday‑life or productivity‑focused psychology topics (e.g., decision‑making, work habits)
Start each script with a punchy hook question or bold claim within the first 5 seconds
Keep the core content tight—aim for ~30‑second segments rather than 40‑plus seconds
Add a series tag or episode number in the title to signal continuity
Use clear, actionable takeaways and visual cues to reinforce key points
avoid: Abstract or highly academic subjects that lack immediate relevance (e.g., psychoanalysis theory, revolution psychology)
Long, meandering introductions without a clear hook
Titles that are vague or lack a series/episode identifier
full.title_style: Hook with a bold promise or question, then a concise subtitle and a series/episode tag (e.g., “Boost Focus in 30 s – Guided Reading #2”).
next_tests: Compare tight (~30 s) vs. standard (~42 s) video lengths for the same topic
A/B test titles that start with a question vs. a declarative promise
Run a series‑tagged video against a standalone title to measure binge‑watch propensity
